notes:
SMB inbound via self-serve sign-up; trial account created 2026-02-12 with free credits. Initially spinning up a chat-based support assistant (support-agent) that invokes internal tools (ticket lookup, order status). Primary ask: help make streaming + function-calling robust in browser clients and avoid malformed JSON on client parse.

Key pain seen on POC: model emits function call payloads but shape sometimes differs from declared function schema (e.g., 'order_id' as number vs string), and streaming chunks split JSON objects mid-key which our frontend's EventSource/ReadableStream parser chokes on. Frontend team currently uses fetch() + reader.read() to assemble chunks; intermittently sees trailing commas or partial arrays, causing JSON.parse failures.

Customer quote (CTO): "We love the latency on hosted API but if the function schema isn't stable we'll have to stop streaming and increase roundtrips — that blows up cost."

They asked for: sample browser SDK snippet that shows safe reassembly of SSE/Fetch streamed JSON objects, recommended schema enforcement strategies, and guidance on using Redwood's function-calling vs explicit JSON-mode structured output. Also want notes on how to detect and recover from mid-stream schema mismatches (fallback to non-streaming call, server-side revalidation, schema coercion examples).

Security: SOC2 required, SSO planned (Okta). Data residency not strict for now (public cloud is fine). Budget sensitivity: SMB; likely commit if streaming is stable and sample code reduces dev time.

Sales angle: PLG lead converting to AE outreach; emphasize quick wins: 1) share troubleshooting doc + snippets, 2) runtime flags to enforce strict schema or cause model to emit canonical types, 3) short-lived dedicated token config for POC diagnostics.

Other notes: tried competitor X's streaming — had similar issues but competitor had built-in chunk reassembler lib. Elmstone asks if Redwood has one or can supply sample helper code. SE asked to prepare sample repo and lightweight lab run (30-60 min).
